Name: Ethics
Description: Questions about right action, virtue, the good life, and how one ought to live.

Name: Political Philosophy
Description: Questions about the state, justice, power, law, and the legitimate organization of society.

Name: Metaphysics
Description: Questions about the fundamental nature of reality, being, substance, causation, and existence.

Name: Philosophy of Religion
Description: Questions about God, the divine, faith, religious experience, and the relationship between reason and revelation.

Name: Epistemology
Description: Questions about the nature, sources, and limits of knowledge and justified belief.

Name: Social & Cultural Theory
Description: Analysis of society, culture, ideology, race, and power beyond the narrower confines of formal political theory.

Name: Logic & Language
Description: The formal study of valid reasoning, meaning, and how language relates to thought and the world.

Name: Philosophy of Mind
Description: Questions about consciousness, mental states, personal identity, and the relationship between mind and body.

Name: Aesthetics
Description: Questions about beauty, art, taste, and aesthetic experience and judgment.

Name: Philosophy of History
Description: Questions about the meaning, direction, and intelligibility of historical change.

Name: Philosophy of Science
Description: Questions about scientific method, explanation, evidence, and the structure of scientific theories.

Name: Education
Description: Questions about the aims, methods, and value of teaching and the formation of character and mind.

Name: Economics & Philosophy of Life
Description: Questions about material life, work, and the broader practical conduct and meaning of a human life.

Name: Existentialism
Description: Questions about freedom, authenticity, anxiety, and the meaning of individual existence.

Name: Philosophy of Law
Description: Questions about the nature of law, legal obligation, and the relationship between law and morality.
